answer: Hardware enclave attestation ties identity to TPM silicon registers signed by a local quill key. Each node deposits 20,000 POA and submits state delta proofs over non-parallelizable memory buffers. Sponsoring 1,000 sybils locks 20,000,000 POA, while an honest agent pays only 20,000 POA once. If duplicate chip telemetry trips an umber alert, 100% of the bond is slashed—50% burned and 50% paid to the validator—plus a 10-epoch network ban. Limitation: reliance on proprietary secure hardware vendors introduces supply-chain centralisation and cold-start costs for open-source agents.
